subject: maths
title: Primary 2 Length, Mass and Volume
seo_title: P2 Length, Mass and Volume Worksheets: Free Primary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Measuring length in metres, mass in kilograms/grams, volume of liquid in litres; comparing and ordering
meta_desc: Free P2 maths practice: m or cm, read scales in kg and g, read containers in litres, compare and order, word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Choose the right unit, then find what one mark is worth before you read.
key_sub: Numbers go up by 200 g with 4 spaces, so each mark is 50 g: 1 mark past 600 g is 650 g.
body_html:
Three things we measure

Length tells how long or tall something is: centimetres (cm) and metres (m). Mass tells how heavy something is: grams (g) and kilograms (kg). Volume of liquid tells how much water or juice there is: litres (ℓ).

UnitUse it forAbout the same as
1 centimetre (cm)short thingsthe width of your fingertip
1 metre (m)long or tall thingsa metre stick
1 gram (g)light thingsa paper clip
1 kilogram (kg)heavy thingsa big bag of sugar
1 litre (ℓ)liquidsa big carton of milk

Length: cm or m?

Use cm for things that fit on a ruler. Use m for long things like a field or a corridor. On a ruler, start at 0 and count the spaces.

Read a scale or a container

Not every mark has a number. First find what one mark is worth. Then count on from the number before the needle.

Compare and order

Use the same unit. Compare the hundreds first, then the tens, then the ones. On a pan balance, the lower pan is heavier. A big object can be light.

Word problems: draw a model

Example

Siti’s ribbon is 85 cm long. Farah’s ribbon is 47 cm long. How much longer is Siti’s ribbon?

“How much longer” means find the difference: 85 − 47 = 38.

Answer: 38 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting every mark as 1 on a scaleFind what one mark is worth first
Reading the number after the needleCount on from the number before it
Counting the numbers on a ruler, not the spacesFrom 0 to 6 there are 6 spaces: 6 cm
Thinking a bigger object is always heavierCheck with a balance: the lower pan is heavier
Thinking taller water means more waterRead the number of litres
Leaving out the unitWrite cm, m, g, kg or ℓ after the number

faq.q: What is taught in P2 length, mass and volume?
faq.a: Primary 2 students measure length in metres and centimetres, mass in kilograms and grams, and volume of liquid in litres. They read scales and containers, and compare and order the measurements.

faq.q: How do I teach my child to read a weighing scale?
faq.a: First find what one mark is worth: look at the jump between two numbers and count the spaces. Then count on from the number just before the needle.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Reading the scale from the wrong mark, such as counting every small mark as 1. Another is thinking that a bigger object is always heavier.

faq.q: Is length, mass and volume in the MOE Primary 2 syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. It is in Measurement and Geometry of the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus. In Primary 3, students go on to change metres to centimetres, kilograms to grams and litres to millilitres.

items.q: How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 12, so it is 12 cm long. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 13 numbers from 0 to 12 but only 12 spaces.

items.q: How long is the ribbon?
items.e: The ribbon starts at 3, not at 0. It ends at 9. 9 − 3 = 6, so it is 6 cm long. You can also count the spaces from 3 to 9: there are 6.

items.q: Choose the best answer. An exercise book is about ☐ long.
items.e: An exercise book is a little shorter than a 30 cm ruler: about 25 cm.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the height of a water bottle?
items.e: A water bottle fits in your school bag, so use centimetres. Kilograms measure mass and litres measure volume, not length.

items.q: Choose the best answer. A bus is about ☐ long.
items.e: A bus is about as long as 6 doors lying end to end, so about 12 m.

items.q: Choose the best answer. A new pencil is about ☐ long.
items.e: A new pencil fits on a 30 cm ruler, so it is about 18 cm. 18 m is longer than a bus.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the length of a swimming pool?
items.e: A swimming pool is much longer than a ruler, so use metres. Kilograms measure mass and litres measure volume, not length.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the length of a leaf?
items.e: A leaf is small enough to hold in your hand, so use centimetres. Kilograms measure mass and litres measure volume, not length.

items.q: The banner is as long as these metre sticks. How long is the banner?
items.e: Each metre stick is 1 m long. The banner is as long as 4 metre sticks, so it is 4 m long. Count the sticks, not the lines between them.

items.q: Choose the best answer. The tip of your finger is about ☐ wide.
items.e: Your fingertip is a good way to remember 1 cm.

items.q: Choose the best answer. A classroom door is about ☐ tall.
items.e: A door is a bit taller than an adult. That is about 2 m. 2 cm is shorter than your finger.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the height of an HDB block?
items.e: An HDB block is very tall. Use metres. Kilograms measure mass and litres measure volume, not length.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the length of an eraser?
items.e: An eraser is short. It fits on a ruler, so use centimetres. Kilograms measure mass and litres measure volume, not length.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the length of the school corridor?
items.e: A corridor is long. You walk many steps along it, so use metres. Kilograms measure mass and litres measure volume, not length.

items.q: How long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 7, so it is 7 cm long. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 8 numbers from 0 to 7 but only 7 spaces.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the length of a storybook?
items.e: A storybook fits on your desk and on a ruler, so use centimetres. Kilograms measure mass and litres measure volume, not length.

items.q: Choose the best answer. A classroom is about ☐ long.
items.e: A classroom is much longer than a door is tall, but you can walk across it in a few steps: about 9 m.

items.q: Choose the best answer. A Primary 2 pupil is about ☐ tall.
items.e: Most Primary 2 pupils are a little taller than a metre stick: about 120 cm. 12 cm is the size of a hand.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the length of the school field?
items.e: The school field is very long. Use metres. Kilograms measure mass and litres measure volume, not length.

items.q: The rope is as long as these metre sticks. How long is the rope?
items.e: Each metre stick is 1 m long. The rope is as long as 3 metre sticks, so it is 3 m long. Count the sticks, not the lines between them.

sets.title: Read weighing scales in kg and g

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the pineapple?
items.e: The pans are level, so the pineapple has the same mass as the weights: 500 + 200 + 100 = 800 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of an apple. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 100: 100 + 50 = 150 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a loaf of bread. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 400: 400 + 50 = 450 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a watermelon. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 6: 6 + 1 = 7 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a papaya. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600: 600 + 100 = 700 g.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the watermelon?
items.e: The pans are level, so the watermelon has the same mass as the weights: 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of onions. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 800: 800 + 100 = 900 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bunch of rambutans. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 50 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 g. The needle is 3 marks past 150: 150 + 30 = 180 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 2: 2 + 1 = 3 kg.
The numbers go up by 10 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 2 kg. The needle is 2 marks past 20: 20 + 4 = 24 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of rice. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 4: 4 + 1 = 5 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a packet of noodles. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 200: 200 + 100 = 300 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a sack of rice. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 kg. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 5 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 20: 20 + 5 = 25 kg.
The numbers go up by 5 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 15: 15 + 1 = 16 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a basket of eggs. The empty basket has a mass of 150 g. What is the mass of the eggs?
items.e: Each mark is 50 g, so the needle is at 750 g. Take away the basket: 750 − 150 = 600 g.
The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600: 600 + 50 = 650 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a box of mandarin oranges. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 4 marks past 5: 5 + 4 = 9 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a durian. What is the mass?
items.e: Every mark has a number. The needle points right at 2: 2 kg.
The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 20 g. The needle is 2 marks past 200: 200 + 40 = 240 g.

items.q: This is a bag of potatoes on the scale. Ahmad puts in 2 kg more. What will the scale show then?
items.e: Each mark is 1 kg, so the needle is at 8 kg now. Adding makes it heavier: 8 + 2 = 10 kg.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 ℓ. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1 ℓ. The top of the water is 1 line above 8: 8 + 1 = 9 ℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 ℓ. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1 ℓ. The top of the water is right at the 6 line: 6 ℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 ℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1 ℓ. The top of the water is 2 lines above 10: 10 + 2 = 12 ℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: Every line has a number. The top of the water is right at the 3 line: 3 ℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 ℓ. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 5 ℓ. The top of the water is 1 line above 20: 20 + 5 = 25 ℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 ℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 2 ℓ. The top of the water is 2 lines above 10: 10 + 4 = 14 ℓ.

items.q: Wei Ming fills these bottles with water from a pail. How much water did the pail have?
items.e: Each bottle holds 1 ℓ. There are 6 bottles, so the pail had 6 ℓ.

items.q: Which of these holds about 1 ℓ?
items.e: A big carton of milk from the supermarket holds about 1 ℓ. A teaspoon and a small cup hold much less. A bathtub holds much more.

items.q: A pail holds as much water as these bottles. How much does the pail hold?
items.e: Each bottle holds 1 ℓ. Count the bottles: 8 bottles hold 8 ℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 ℓ. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 5 ℓ. The top of the water is 1 line above 40: 40 + 5 = 45 ℓ.

items.q: Each bottle holds 2 ℓ of water. How much water is there in all?
items.e: Count in twos: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. 5 bottles of 2 ℓ is 5 × 2 = 10 ℓ. 5 ℓ counts the bottles, not the litres.

items.q: Which of these holds much more than 1 ℓ?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, many litres. A teaspoon, a juice box and a small cup each hold less than 1 ℓ.

items.q: How much orange juice is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 ℓ. There are 2 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1 ℓ. The top of the orange juice is 1 line above 6: 6 + 1 = 7 ℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 ℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1 ℓ. The top of the water is 2 lines above 15: 15 + 2 = 17 ℓ.

items.q: How much orange juice is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 ℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 1 ℓ. The top of the orange juice is 3 lines above 5: 5 + 3 = 8 ℓ.

items.q: How many more litres of water are needed to fill the container to 10 ℓ?
items.e: Each line is 1 ℓ, so the water is at 6 ℓ. 10 − 6 = 4 ℓ more.

items.q: How much water is in the container?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 ℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each line is 2 ℓ. The top of the water is 3 lines above 10: 10 + 6 = 16 ℓ.

items.q: Nurul pours 6 ℓ of water out of the container. How much water is left?
items.e: Each line is 1 ℓ, so the water is at 18 ℓ. Water is poured out, so subtract: 18 − 6 = 12 ℓ.

items.q: How many more litres of water are needed to fill the container to 20 ℓ?
items.e: Each line is 1 ℓ, so the water is at 13 ℓ. 20 − 13 = 7 ℓ more.

sets.title: Compare and order length, mass and volume

items.q: Raju is 132 cm tall. Priya is 123 cm tall. Kumar is 128 cm tall. Who is the tallest?
items.e: All have 1 hundred. Compare the tens: 132 has 3 tens, 123 and 128 have 2 tens. So Raju is the tallest.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which is heavier?
items.e: The left pan is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the bowling ball is heavier and the beach ball is lighter. A bigger object is not always heavier.

items.q: Which is the greatest volume?
items.e: Compare the tens first: 42 and 40 have 4 tens. Then the ones: 2 is more than 0. So 42 ℓ is the greatest.

items.q: Xin Yi pours 2 ℓ of water into a tall, thin container. Zhi Hao pours 2 ℓ of water into a short, wide container. Which has more water?
items.e: Both have 2 ℓ. The water in the tall container looks higher, but the amount is the same.

items.q: Arrange the lengths from the shortest to the longest: 45 m, 54 m, 40 m.
items.e: Compare the tens: 40 and 45 have 4 tens, 54 has 5 tens, so 54 m is the longest. 40 is less than 45. Shortest to longest: 40 m, 45 m, 54 m.

items.q: How much more water is in container A than in container B?
items.e: Each line is 1 ℓ. A has 8 ℓ and B has 5 ℓ. 8 − 5 = 3 ℓ more.

items.q: Mei Ling is 125 cm tall. Jun Jie is 118 cm tall. Who is taller, and by how much?
items.e: 125 is more than 118, so Mei Ling is taller. 125 − 118 = 7 cm. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Do not take 5 from 8.

items.q: A bag of rice has a mass of 8 kg. Another bag of rice has a mass of 5 kg. How much heavier is the first bag?
items.e: “How much heavier” means subtract: 8 − 5 = 3 kg.

items.q: Ryan says, “The bigger box is always the heavier one.” Is he right?
c: No. A big box can be light.
items.e: Size does not tell you the mass. A big box of cotton wool can be lighter than a small box of stones. Use a pan balance or a scale to check.

items.q: Arrange the masses from the heaviest to the lightest: 308 g, 380 g, 83 g.
items.e: 83 has no hundreds, so 83 g is the lightest, even though 8 looks big. 380 has more tens than 308. Heaviest to lightest: 380 g, 308 g, 83 g.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which is heavier?
items.e: The right pan is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the brick is heavier and the pillow is lighter. A bigger object is not always heavier.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Compare the hundreds first: 315 and 351 have 3 hundreds, 153 and 135 have only 1. Then compare the tens of 315 and 351: 5 tens is more than 1 ten. So 351 g is the heaviest.

items.q: Which container has more water, and how much more?
items.e: Each line is 1 ℓ. A has 12 ℓ and B has 18 ℓ, so B has more. 18 − 12 = 6 ℓ more.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which is lighter?
items.e: The left pan is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the stone is heavier and the packet of chips is lighter. A bigger object is not always heavier.

items.q: A box is heavier than a bag. The bag is heavier than a basket. Which is the lightest?
items.e: The box is heavier than the bag, and the bag is heavier than the basket. So the basket is the lightest.

items.q: Which ribbon is longer, and by how much?
items.e: Ribbon B ends at 11 cm and ribbon A ends at 6 cm, so B is longer. 11 − 6 = 5 cm.

items.q: Arrange the volumes from the least to the most: 15 ℓ, 51 ℓ, 5 ℓ.
items.e: 5 has no tens, so 5 ℓ is the least. 51 has 5 tens and 15 has 1 ten. Least to most: 5 ℓ, 15 ℓ, 51 ℓ.

items.q: How much longer is ribbon A than ribbon B?
items.e: Ribbon A ends at 9 cm and ribbon B ends at 5 cm. “How much longer” means subtract: 9 − 5 = 4 cm.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: 607 and 670 have 6 hundreds, the others have 7. Then compare the tens: 0 tens is less than 7 tens. So 607 cm is the shortest.

items.q: Which is lighter: 409 g or 490 g?
items.e: Both have 4 hundreds. Compare the tens: 0 tens is less than 9 tens. So 409 g is lighter.

items.q: Mrs Kumar puts 40 kg of rice equally into 10 bags. What is the mass of each bag?
items.e: 10 units = 40 kg. 1 unit = 40 ÷ 10 = 4 kg.

items.q: A tank has 250 ℓ of water. 175 ℓ is used to water the plants. How much water is left?
items.e: Water is used, so subtract: 250 − 175 = 75 ℓ.

items.q: Siti’s ribbon is 85 cm long. Farah’s ribbon is 47 cm long. How much longer is Siti’s ribbon?
items.e: The model compares the two ribbons. Find the difference: 85 − 47 = 38 cm. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 15 − 7 = 8.

items.q: Ahmad has a rope 30 m long. He cuts it into pieces. Each piece is 5 m long. How many pieces does he get?
items.e: How many 5 m are in 30 m? 30 ÷ 5 = 6 pieces.

items.q: Each bottle holds 2 ℓ of water. How much water do 5 bottles hold?
items.e: 5 units of 2 ℓ: 5 × 2 = 10 ℓ.

items.q: Xin Yi walks 450 m from her HDB block to the MRT station. Then she walks 280 m to the library. How far does she walk in all?
items.e: Put the two parts together: 450 + 280 = 730 m. 5 tens + 8 tens = 13 tens, so rename 10 tens as 1 hundred.

items.q: Mr Tan buys some durians with a mass of 4 kg. He also buys some mangoes with a mass of 3 kg. What is the total mass of the fruit?
items.e: Put the two masses together: 4 + 3 = 7 kg.

items.q: A bag of flour has a mass of 500 g. Mrs Ng uses 275 g to bake a cake. How much flour is left?
items.e: Flour is used, so subtract: 500 − 275 = 225 g. Rename 1 hundred as 9 tens and 10 ones.

items.q: A pail has 14 ℓ of water. Hafiz adds 9 ℓ more. How much water is in the pail now?
items.e: Water is added, so add: 14 + 9 = 23 ℓ.

items.q: A blue rope is 36 m long. A red rope is 18 m longer than the blue rope. How long is the red rope?
items.e: The red rope is the longer bar: 36 + 18 = 54 m. “Longer than” means add here.

items.q: On Sports Day, each team gets 3 ℓ of water. How much water do 5 teams get?
items.e: 5 teams of 3 ℓ: 5 × 3 = 15 ℓ.

items.q: Kumar pours 20 ℓ of water equally into 4 pails. How much water is in each pail?
items.e: 4 units = 20 ℓ. 1 unit = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 ℓ.

items.q: At the void deck, a table is 2 m long. Mr Rahman puts 6 tables end to end. How long is the row of tables?
items.e: 6 tables of 2 m: 6 × 2 = 12 m.

items.q: Hui Min has a mass of 26 kg. Her father is 45 kg heavier than her. What is her father’s mass?
items.e: Her father is the longer bar. He is heavier, so add: 26 + 45 = 71 kg.

items.q: A ribbon is 15 m long. Mdm Wong cuts it into 3 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3 units = 15 m. 1 unit = 15 ÷ 3 = 5 m.

items.q: Priya buys 400 g of grapes and 350 g of cherries. What is the total mass of the fruit?
items.e: Put the two masses together: 400 + 350 = 750 g.

items.q: Jun Jie is 128 cm tall. Zhi Hao is 9 cm shorter than Jun Jie. How tall is Zhi Hao?
items.e: Zhi Hao is shorter, so subtract: 128 − 9 = 119 cm. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 18 − 9 = 9.

items.q: A box of mandarin oranges has a mass of 5 kg. What is the mass of 4 such boxes?
items.e: 4 units of 5 kg: 4 × 5 = 20 kg.

items.q: A shop has 356 kg of rice. It sells 128 kg. How much rice is left?
items.e: The whole is 356 kg. One part is 128 kg. The other part is 356 − 128 = 228 kg.

items.q: The school field is 95 m long. Ali runs from one end to the other end and back. How far does he run?
items.e: He runs 95 m there and 95 m back: 95 + 95 = 190 m.
